name: artamatch-children-five-aspect-12
zodiac: sidereal (Lahiri), noon UT, birth dates only
target_says: whether the historical record lists children for a couple like this
target_question: did the historical record list children for a couple like this
formula: score = bias + SUM over 12 angles of SUM over the five Ptolemaic aspects A of w[angle,A] * cos(angle - A);   p = sigmoid(score)
cv_note: nested 10-fold: which angles enter and the ridge lambda were re-run inside every training fold, and the fast bodies were forced in inside every fold, so this number never saw its own test couples. The five aspect angles are FIXED, not fitted.

decomposition.note: Restrict every family to Sun..Saturn and the model falls from 0.6911 to 0.5486; restrict it to Sun..Mars and it reaches 0.4955. Two parameters of the husband's birth year alone reach 0.6747 of the model's 0.6912. The seven fast-body angles the model is required to carry hold 11% of its total strength between them.

aspects.why_balanced_matters: SUM_A exp(2iA) = 0 for these five angles, so A'A = (5/2)I and the penalty they induce on each angle is exactly (2/5)*lambda*I. Ridge is NOT invariant to the choice of aspect basis, so this balance is what makes writing the model in these five harmless.
aspects.identity: w[angle,A] = (2/5)*amp*cos(A - ideal_separation), and SUM_A w[angle,A]*cos(theta-A) = amp*cos(theta - ideal_separation). Each angle is therefore TWO numbers: how strongly it matters, and the separation it prefers. Conjunction and opposition are always exact negatives because cos(theta-180) = -cos(theta).

solver.method: damped Newton on the ridge-penalised logistic objective
solver.note: log-loss plus a positive ridge is strictly convex, so the minimum is unique and does not depend on the starting point; every Newton step is one Cholesky solve, halved until the penalised loss falls.

within_era.note: Inside a single husband-birth decade, couple-weighted: the model reaches 0.5673 where two numbers of age gap reach 0.5662, and handing the age gap to the model moves it to 0.5671. It adds nothing, because the model already contains it: the angle between two slow planets IS the gap between the two birth dates, wrapped round a circle. One partner's chart alone is chance within era (0.4950 his, 0.5132 hers).

families.note: pair_only is false; the solo families present are aspM, aspW, midW. Self-sums (i=j in midM/midW, a doubled longitude rather than a midpoint) were removed from the bank: they cost nothing measurable and read as nonsense.

size_choice.rule: the smallest model that loses nothing on the honest metric. Pooled AUC keeps climbing with more angles (0.69115 at 12 -> 0.69269 at 28) but the WITHIN-ERA figure peaks at 10-12 angles and then flattens (0.56733 at 12 vs 0.56689 at 28). The angles past the twelfth buy pooled AUC only, which is to say they buy more birth calendar, so they were left out and the model is less than half the size to read.
